correctness.rationale: The inner horizontal-chord domain ends at the unique parameter-dependent discriminant zero between sqrt(8/3) and sqrt(3), not the zero-parameter circle height. The area is exactly twice the positive-side discriminant square-root integral. A two-endpoint matched expansion proves the 10 log(lambda)/lambda coefficient and the finite constant 5+2 log(243/256), while dominated convergence and the unit-Jacobian Rayleigh/van der Pol map establish the outer area coefficient. The small-damping coefficient follows by dominated convergence after rationalization; Simpson/bisection script verify.py replayed with CHECK_OK. Finite numerics do not replace analytic limits.

value.rationale: The pair of published, canonically specified trapping ovals bounds a unique Rayleigh limit cycle, so their enclosed-area ratio is a natural quantitative measure of geometric certificate coarseness. The exact high-damping fraction approximately 1/40 versus the weak-damping limit 1/3 gives a motivated benchmark for later sharpened algebraic traps. The delicate contribution from both ends of the moving discriminant interval supplies a nontrivial sharp logarithmic correction, not a textbook direct substitution. The result does not overclaim the limit-cycle area or certificate optimality.
